prompt:
The graph below shows sales of books in three formats in one country between 2010 and 2024.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
instruction_line: You should spend about 20 minutes on this task. Write at least 150 words.

visual.title: Sales of printed books, e-books and audiobooks, 2010-2024
visual.alt: A line chart showing the change in sales of printed books, e-books and audiobooks in millions of units from 2010 to 2024.

key_points: Printed books remain the best-selling format throughout the period but do not follow a steady trend: they fall from 92 million to 58 million in 2019, then recover to 66 million
E-books first rise sharply (8 → 55 million), peak in 2019, then fall back to 44 million — the only peak-and-decline pattern
Audiobooks grow continuously throughout the period; rising from 2 million to 62 million, more than a thirty-fold increase, making them the fastest-growing format
The only crossover happens between 2022 and 2024: audiobooks overtake e-books (from 45 vs 48 to 62 vs 44) and move into second place
The gap between the three formats narrows: in 2010 there was a 90-million gap between the highest and lowest, falling to 22 million by 2024
Total sales rise in every year measured (from roughly 102 million to 172 million)
common_mistakes: Giving an opinion or inventing a cause ('people stopped reading because of phones')
Reading out all eighteen data points one by one instead of summarising the three main trends (printed: decline then recovery, e-books: peak then decline, audiobooks: continuous growth)
Skipping the crossover and the change in ranking — the most striking event in the chart
Dropping the million unit ('sales fell to 58') or confusing it with a percentage
Extrapolating beyond where the chart ends ('audiobooks will soon overtake printed books')
